featured_reviews.review_text: Great place to fill your vehicle with petrol and diesel or CNG if required.... featured_reviews.name: Anupam Sil
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are definitely billing issues here, especially with petrol cars. Beware of filling without physically getting down to check the zero set. The staff has various tricks to divert your attention and start the fill without zero set, thereby you end up with less petrol. Done more often if the vehicle in front is a bike which fills a small amount of petrol and therefore you cannot confirm if the reading is right or wrong. Fuel quality is good, I fill here every two days for the past 8 years but never break the routine of getting down and ensuring zero set.

Recent update of photos, this happened on 25th June 2018, caught them red handed. Look closely you can see how he has kept the nozzle in the adjacent compartment so that there is no zero set happening before the operator starts filling for you.

All I did was look slightly to one side when he completed filling the small material carrier in front of me who filled about Rs.100 of diesel. Immediately the operator kept the nozzle to the side waiting for my car to come into position.

Please learn and ensure you have a strict routine of getting down and seeing the zero set to avoid being duped.

Next time you stop to fill air in your tyres, stay alert. A common trick is happening at some air pumps:

💨 Air slowly leaks out…
⚠️ Then he tells you, “tyre is punctured.”

Right beside the pump, another person (part of the same scam) will quickly offer to “fix” it and charge ₹200–₹300 to replace the valve — even though nothing was actually wrong.

🛑 How to protect yourself:
• Watch closely while air is being filled
• Check the valve yourself before agreeing to any repair
• Don’t rush into paying for “quick fixes”
• If possible, fill air yourself

👉 Stay alert. Share this post to help others avoid getting scammed!

I had a very concerning experience at Anuradha Gas Station (Indian Oil), JVLR Andheri East.

On 15 June 2026, I filled petrol and the staff initially told me the bill amount was around ₹3,491. I was surprised because I had observed the meter and expected the amount to be around ₹2,700. After questioning them, they produced a bill showing ₹3,391, and I ended up paying the amount through UPI.

Later, when I reached home and checked the receipt carefully, I noticed that the receipt time was 20:41, whereas my UPI payment was made at 21:13. This clearly indicated that the receipt did not belong to my transaction. I immediately returned to the petrol pump, and after discussion, the staff admitted it was a "mistake" and refunded the excess amount.

What makes this even more suspicious is that during a previous visit, I witnessed another customer arguing that petrol had not been filled into his vehicle despite being charged.

Such incidents raise serious concerns about transparency and customer trust. Customers should carefully verify the meter reading, receipt details, and transaction amount before making payment. The management and authorities should investigate these repeated complaints and take strict action if any fraudulent practices are found.

I have preserved the receipt and payment proof and will continue to raise this issue with the appropriate authorities if necessary.

Date of Incident: 15 June 2026
Location: Anuradha Gas Station, JVLR, Andheri East, Mumbai

I usually prefer filling petrol at Indian Oil petrol pumps, but yesterday I had a rather disappointing experience. While returning home, I stopped at this petrol station to fill fuel in my car.

The man filling the petrol suddenly started asking, “Where in UP are you from?” At first, we thought he was speaking to someone else, but when he repeated the question, Arvind — my brother’s friend who was driving — replied, “Varanasi.” After that, he continued asking more personal questions, and in the middle of the conversation, he suddenly said, “Auto cut ho gaya hai.”

We had asked for petrol worth ₹1005, but when I looked carefully, the meter had already shown two lines before the filling even started. He then claimed the machine had auto-cut at ₹840 and returned the remaining amount because I had already paid ₹1005 in advance. Even while returning the balance, the amount was ₹5 short.

What felt even stranger was that once we started driving, the fuel indicator in the car barely moved up. Only God knows what actually happened.

Overall, the entire experience left me feeling cheated and deeply disappointed. It is sad how, at times, people compromise their honesty and integrity for such small gains. Trust is something customers carry with them when they stop at a fuel station, and once broken, it leaves a very unpleasant feeling behind.

Ironically, my name is also Anuradha, and coincidentally, the gas station was called “Anuradha Gas Station.”

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the petrol pump on 25 March 2026 at around 9:40 PM. During refueling, a staff member named Devesh attended my vehicle. He was not wearing an ID card and was also not in proper uniform, which itself is against standard operating procedures.

While filling fuel, there appeared to be no auto-cut functioning on the dispensing unit. I repeatedly requested him to stop as the tank was getting full, but he ignored my instructions and continued filling. This resulted in approximately 200 ml (or more) fuel spilling over my vehicle, causing wastage and potential safety hazard.

When I politely asked him why the fuel was overfilled and who would compensate for the spilled fuel, he responded in an arrogant and disrespectful manner, saying “jitna meter me hua hai utna pay kar aur nikal.” When I objected to his behavior, he made a rude gesture and asked me to leave.

Later, the owner/manager Mr. Anil Singh came. I explained the entire situation to him. Instead of addressing the issue professionally or apologizing, he casually stated that the worker had been working for 12 hours and was frustrated. This is not an acceptable justification.

If a staff member is working continuously for 12 hours and is not in a proper condition to serve customers safely, then it is the management’s responsibility to ensure proper shift rotation. Allowing fatigued staff to handle fuel dispensing is dangerous and negligent, as it can lead to spillage, fire hazard, and customer disputes.

Further, when I requested the complaint/feedback register, they refused to provide it and asked me to leave, which is highly unprofessional and against customer rights.

This incident appears to violate the following:

Consumer Protection Act, 2019 – deficiency in service and unfair behavior.
Legal Metrology (Weights & Measures) Rules – improper dispensing and non-functioning auto-cut.
Petroleum Rules & Safety Guidelines – unsafe fuel handling and spillage.
Mandatory requirement to maintain and provide complaint register at fuel outlets.
I request HPCL to kindly:

Investigate this incident thoroughly.
Take strict action against the staff for misconduct.
Ensure proper working auto-cut mechanism in dispensing units.
Ensure all staff wear ID cards and proper uniforms.
Ensure staff are not made to work excessively long shifts affecting safety.
Instruct the outlet to maintain and provide a complaint register.
Take corrective measures to avoid such incidents in future.
This matter involves customer safety, fuel wastage, and misconduct, and therefore requires urgent attention.
